issues.note: Six protocol revisions are pinned: the SDK's five negotiable legacy revisions (2024-10-07, 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25) reached via the initialize handshake, and 2026-07-28 reached via server/discover plus the per-request _meta envelope. tests/protocol/conformanceMatrix.ts declares one explicit cell per revision x behavior; tests/protocol/conformance.test.ts drives the real createMcpHandler once per pinned cell across ten behaviors (revision negotiation, capability negotiation, undeclared capabilities staying unserved, tool surface, tool schemas, error vocabulary, era-specific result fields, cancellation, JSON-RPC batching, Streamable HTTP transport) = 60 conformant cells. Not-pinned is a third state, never collapsed into either result: resolveCell reaches 'conformant' only from a pinned declaration whose fixture ran AND passed, a pinned cell with no executing fixture resolves to 'unproven' and fails the gate, and MCP Tasks / MCP Apps are declared not_pinned with reasons rather than omitted. scripts/conformance-matrix.ts is the gate — it binds vitest results back to cells via the [conformance <revision> <behavior>] token and fails on an unproven cell, a failing cell, an orphan fixture, a failed check bound to no cell (how revision drift surfaces), or a stale docs/PROTOCOL_CONFORMANCE.md. All four failure modes were exercised live before landing. CI runs the gate as a named step in .github/workflows/ci.yml. The published matrix names revisions and behaviors and quotes no coverage percentage, and keeps supported / merged / conformance-proven apart.

issues.note: src/lib/runnerEligibility.ts judges seven capability dimensions (runtime location, credential custody, network exposure, lifecycle control, cancellation, audit trail, approval enforcement) against a declared posture, as a strict attended < unattended < public ratchet. Absent evidence and negative evidence never share a code path: no record scores unproven -> needs_evidence, a negative record scores refuted -> ineligible. An attestation without a source counts in neither direction; a malformed record is absence, never a refusal. Fails closed — no/empty/malformed profile returns needs_evidence, and no input yields eligible without a positive sourced record for every required dimension. Reachability is recorded but is deliberately not an input to the decision. export_build_brief takes runner_posture (default 'public'), runner_reachable, and runner_capability_profile, and exports the decision plus per-dimension evidence as the runner_eligibility field and in §9 for runner-hostable targets only. Presence/absence fixture pairs cover every required dimension at every posture. Compact-response size ceiling raised 90 KB -> 96 KB deliberately: the canonical compact response was already at 98.3% of the old budget, so the evidence could not fit under it.

issues.note: Found by LAB's promotion-queue session (/promote, orchestratelab PR #58) by doing it and reverting: promoting a playbook past its still-candidate golden-path route made loadRegistry({ includeBeta: true }) throw 'Unknown route id' for EVERY caller (not just the one playbook), and validate_playbook_candidate read playbooks only — nothing in the MCP could certify a route at all. Fixed both halves, the atomic-pair option (not 'route inherits playbook certification'), since it is the one that keeps loadRegistry structurally unbreakable by a half-promotion. (1) src/registry/registryValidation.ts + registryAssembly.ts: validateCrossReferences resolves golden_path_route_id against the full unfiltered route set first; a route that exists but is invisible only at the current status filter is now a severity:'warning' entry that never fails a strict load (a genuinely unknown route id is still a hard error). (2) A new CI/lint gate, lintPlaybookRouteStatusOrder in registryLint.ts, makes the drift impossible to land in the first place. It deliberately does NOT use a raw status-rank comparison: src/registry/lifecycleStatus.ts's routeLagsBehindPlaybook models the real constraint that beta/candidate are gated behind two INDEPENDENT loadRegistry flags (includeBeta, includeCandidates) while published/validated need neither — a naive rank check was caught live wrongly flagging 7 real 'published' playbooks pointing at merely-'validated' routes (both load with zero flags, always fine) before it shipped. (3) validate_playbook_candidate gained an optional route_yaml input: supplying it certifies the playbook + route pair together, reporting pair_qualifies_for as the lower of each side's own structural DoD ceiling, and pair_status_mismatch:true with a plain blocking sentence — never a throw — when the playbook's declared status is already ahead of its route's. Locked by tests/registry/registryLoader.test.ts (drives the exact LAB failure plus a regression guard for a truly-unknown route id), tests/registry/registryLint.test.ts (the new gate, including the published/validated non-violation case), and 7 new cases in tests/tools/validatePlaybookCandidate.test.ts. pnpm verify: 2358/2358.

Goal-constraint phrase tables were matched with bare String.includes, so a phrase sitting inside a longer word counted as if the user had written it. 'posts the result in the same THREAD ONLY after I approve' contains 'read only' (th-read only) and fired the read-only prohibition on a goal that explicitly asks the agent to POST, degrading constraint_label to gaps; 'unread only', 'spread only', 'thread-only', 'no written approval' and 'preview before' (vs the approval phrase 'review before') failed the same way. Matching is now whole-word via (?<!\w)...(?!\w) lookarounds in src/lib/constraintSignals.ts, shared by constraintCoverage's own firstMatch. Inflections that substring matching had covered implicitly are now ENUMERATED in the tables (never writes, never edits/editing, never commits/committing) so a reader can see exactly what fires. The chat_triggered_assistant golden fixture's coverage_tags: ['read_only'] was a mislabel produced by this bug and is corrected.

An Airtable WRITE goal was planned as a READ. airtable_lookup is read-only (permissions.write is [], Connect entry 'Airtable - read base', required scopes data.records:read / schema.bases:read), but the bare `airtable` KEYWORD_HINT carried no direction, so 'write the output to an Airtable base' composed scheduled_trigger -> db_read -> airtable_lookup -> ... with NO write component in the route at all, and the plan told the user to provision a read-only token for a task needing writes. Two of four probed write goals were worse: 'append each new lead to our Airtable table' and 'update the status field in Airtable when a deal closes' made crm_note_write (a HubSpot/Salesforce note) the only write in the route - a write to a system the user never named. Fixed with the treatment MAR-254 already gave the SQL source, applied to the provider token that never got it. No new component needed: file_storage's own summary already names 'an Airtable base' as a destination and its Connect entry lists Airtable with API-key auth. A bare 'draft' hijacked non-email goals into email_draft + optional_email_send - an outbound email send on goals that never mention email. 'draft' was simultaneously a DOMAIN_KEYWORDS.email_calendar token and a KEYWORD_HINTS entry pointing at email_draft, so the word established the email domain single-handedly and then fired the hint that domain permits. Live-probed on master 59fbbbc: 'generate 3 headline variants ... compose a review draft ... require my approval' composed ... -> email_draft -> ... -> optional_email_send -> audit_log, and 'draft a product announcement and post it to Slack after I approve' gained an email send alongside the Slack post. MAR-526 slice 5 ROUTED AROUND this - its variant_review goal was worded 'stage for review' instead of 'compose a review draft' specifically to dodge it - so the bug was papered over by fixture wording, not fixed. Two comments in capabilityMatcher.ts already called the word unreliable without wiring it to the general case (STRONG_EMAIL_CALENDAR_TOKENS 'deliberately EXCLUDES draft'; MAR-219's CHAT_OVERLAPPING_EMAIL_KEYWORDS fixed exactly this for chat goals only). Fixed by making 'draft' a WEAK email_calendar trigger - MAR-131's suppressWeakOnlyDomain mechanism, generalising MAR-219 to every other primary domain. A real mailbox goal is untouched: reply/replies/email/gmail/inbox/mailbox/calendar/meeting/invite all stay STRONG. The honest consequence is visible on the card: 'draft a product announcement' now returns coverage 'poor' with unmatched_demand ['draft a product announcement'] - a stated gap (MAR-250) instead of a silently wrong component. RECORDED LIMIT (MAR-529 discipline): a goal whose ONLY domain signal is 'draft' ('draft a weekly update') has no competing primary domain for the suppression to defer to, so email_draft is still selected; separating that needs intent parsing, not lexical de-biasing. Locked by tests/graph/draftScope.test.ts (16 assertions, presence + absence, including an explicit assertion of the residual). Lifecycle flips to 'merged' with the merge commit.

Approval provenance, from LAB's day-one signal intake (MAR-532): five separate partial plans all matched human_approval_gate + audit_log and all missed binding an approval to the exact action executed. ASSESSED AS BOTH a component gap and an edge gap. Mechanism = component gap: the gate's declared output is 'approved | rejected | timeout', a decision with no identity attached to what was decided, and audit_log takes the executed payload with no reference to an approved one, so no consumer can compare them; the drift failure modes appear in neither component's failure_modes (the gate records the HUMAN failing to read, not the system executing something else). Invisibility = edge gap, and it is concrete: of 163 real edges (164 files, one of which is _template.edge.yaml), human_approval_gate has ZERO outgoing edges (13 point at it, none leave it), and its own YAML's recommended_with: audit_log exists in the component file and NOT in the graph - route composition orders these components but never relates them. Sequence is not provenance. Worse than 'no component': a goal explicitly asking for 'an audit trail proving what I approved is exactly what ran' returns approval '✅ enforced' with unmatched_demand [] - a green check no fixture backs. NOT IMPLEMENTED deliberately: the hint-reachable shape is one slice but serves only users who already know to ask, leaving the default overclaim untouched and entrenching the wrong shape; the correct augmenter-injected shape changes every gated plan's route and ripples through the suite, EXPECTED_RELEASE_FINGERPRINT, the MAR-426 manifest fixture, benchmarks/public/*, the golden journeys and the DASH round-trip fixtures - not one slice. Filed with a six-point acceptance bar rather than half-shipped, per MAR-526's own slicing precedent.

The read/write class is still live for two more bare provider tokens, found by generalising MAR-538's fix rather than waiting for a report. Live-probed on the MAR-538/539 branch (e176b29), so NOT regressions from that fix. (a) Stripe: stripe_data_read is read-only and stripe/billing/subscription map to it unconditionally, so 'when a customer asks for a refund, issue the refund in Stripe after I approve it' composes stripe_data_read -> job_queue -> human_approval_gate -> auth_failure_handler. A goal asking to MOVE MONEY gets a plan whose only Stripe step reads data, plus an approval gate guarding an action that is not in the route at all - enforced_approval_gates satisfied with nothing to approve, which is MAR-540's overclaim reached from another direction. No Stripe-write component exists, so unlike Airtable this cannot be solved by re-pointing the hint: either add one, or report the write as unmatched_demand. (b) Postgres/MySQL: MAR-254 fixed the generic half and left the provider half. Its own comment says 'Provider names are domain-unique; the generic forms are direction-carrying PHRASES', treating uniqueness as sufficient when unique is not directional. 'write the processed rows into our Postgres database every night' composes scheduled_trigger -> db_read -> audit_log; 'insert each new record into the mysql table' composes db_read -> schema_validation -> audit_log. Read controls for both providers are correct and must stay correct. Acceptance bar leads with SWEEP not patch: every KEYWORD_HINTS entry whose target component has permissions.write: [] is audited for direction and the result recorded including the entries judged safe - MAR-254, MAR-526 slice 1 and MAR-538 each fixed one token in isolation and nothing ever swept the table. Filed Urgent.
